transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

I have noted the 4C code shown on your Samsung dishwasher display. This step is the right place to begin regardless of that reading, as we need to check if the appliance knows the door is shut. Please close the door firmly and press start. When the door is closed and you press start, does it show the door is open (or a door light stays on)?
The door's closed fine, no door open light or message. When I press start it just beeps and shows 4C again a short while later.

Thanks for letting us know about that. Many dishwashers have a child or control lock, often shown by a key or padlock symbol, which stops the buttons working. The manual shows which buttons to hold to turn it off. Was the child / control lock on (and is it off now), or was it already off?
I don't see any key or padlock symbol on the display, so I don't think the control lock is on. It just beeps and shows 4C a short while after I press start.

Thanks for confirming those details. A delay start, often shown as a countdown like "3h", or a programme that hasn't been confirmed can look like it won't start. Was a delay start set or the programme not selected (and is it sorted), or was nothing like that set?

No delay start was set and no countdown on the display. The programme is selected as normal. It still just beeps and shows 4C a short while after I press start. I should mention there's no water in the tub, and this started after a plumber fitted a new kitchen tap yesterday.

[Heading: Start control]
Thank you for confirming those details. Since the dishwasher has power, recognises the door is closed, and has no child lock or delay start active, but still refuses to start, the issue lies with the start control system. This requires assessment by an appliance engineer. Please note that I am not recommending a specific part at this stage; this diagnosis simply indicates where the fault likely resides so you can arrange appropriate professional help.
